principles: User intent is the contract; five milestones must remain countable through DONE.
Active Proofbound surfaces must use local assurance/admissibility vocabulary, not Authority Server vocabulary.
Legacy compatibility may exist only behind explicit quarantine/whitelist and must not leak into active help/docs/gates.
Scanner evidence must be stronger than prose claims.
drivers: Prevent another DONE overclaim where a narrowed story passes while the original milestones remain incomplete.
Remove confusing Authority Server semantics from the active CLI product surface.

options.name: A: hard physical removal plus explicit legacy quarantine and scanner
pros: Creates machine-verifiable proof for all five milestones
Keeps necessary local evidence features while removing server-backed surfaces
cons: May require careful import cleanup and legacy doc whitelist

options.name: B: only update user-facing wording and keep code/tests as-is
C: delete every file containing authority words with no quarantine
pros: Aggressive cleanup and simpler word scan
cons: Could remove local features or historical docs that still need explicit retired context

chosen: A: hard physical removal plus explicit legacy quarantine and scanner
rationale: Choose A because the user explicitly asked for five milestones without discount until DONE. The implementation must remove or quarantine server-backed Authority surfaces while preserving local proof features, and a hard scanner is needed so completion is mechanically checkable.

preMortem.scenario: The story again narrows to wording-only cleanup
preMortem.trigger: Checklist items are marked done using prose evidence instead of scanner/build/help outputs
preMortem.consequence: DONE passes but M4/M5 remain incomplete
preMortem.mitigation: Each checklist item must cite concrete commands, including retired-Authority scanner, command catalog/help inspection, build, and validate.

preMortem.scenario: Physical deletion breaks local proof features
preMortem.trigger: Authority-named legacy modules share types or helpers with local quorum/admissibility paths
preMortem.consequence: Build or validation fails, or local assurance commands regress
preMortem.mitigation: Trace imports before deletion, quarantine only server-backed surfaces, and preserve local quorum_submit/proof-admissibility/receipt-bundle/delivery-check tests.

preMortem.scenario: Scanner blocks legitimate legacy history forever
preMortem.trigger: No whitelist distinction between active docs/code and retired migration appendices
preMortem.consequence: Useful historical context becomes impossible to keep and validation becomes noisy
preMortem.mitigation: Define explicit whitelist paths/sections and require all other active surfaces to pass hard scanner.

preMortem.scenario: CLI help still leaks old vocabulary
preMortem.trigger: Command descriptions or process-fact policy reasons are not covered by scanner inputs
preMortem.consequence: User still sees Authority wording despite code cleanup
preMortem.mitigation: Scanner must include generated help/catalog text and docs/prompts, not just source files.
